key_errors: 23 jobs remained status="queued" with conclusion=null at run completion (created_at as late as 2026-11-11T20:19:04Z, never started_at)
Upstream jobs Smart_CI and Build / Build both completed with conclusion=success (Build took ~57 minutes, 19:21-20:18)
root_cause: The Windows (VS 2022, Python 3.11, Release) run's Build job succeeded, but every downstream test/packaging job targeting self-hosted Windows runner pools (labels aks-win-4-cores-8gb, aks-win-8-cores-16gb-test, aks-win-4-cores-8gb-test, aks-win-4-cores-8gb-build, and self-hosted/Windows/ptl for GPU) stayed in the queued state and were never picked up by a runner before the overall workflow run was marked as failed. This is consistent with the shared self-hosted Windows runner pool being exhausted or temporarily unavailable (e.g., autoscaler lag, runner registration failure, or an outage in the AKS-backed Windows runner fleet) rather than any code or test defect, since no job logs exist to analyze (jobs never started) and the only two jobs that did execute (Smart_CI on ubuntu-latest, Build on a presumably different/available pool) completed successfully.
reproduction_steps: N/A - not reproducible locally; this is a CI runner-infrastructure capacity/availability issue specific to the self-hosted Windows runner pools used by this workflow.
recommended_actions: Check the self-hosted Windows runner fleet (AKS-backed aks-win-* pools and the dedicated GPU 'ptl' runner) health/capacity dashboards around 2026-11-11T19:21-21:00Z for scaling failures, registration errors, or outages.
Verify the GitHub Actions runner autoscaler/controller logs for the aks-win-* runner scale sets to confirm whether pods failed to register as available runners.
If capacity was simply insufficient, consider increasing the Windows runner pool size or adding queue-depth alerting so a stuck-queue condition is caught before the workflow times out as failure.
Confirm whether the workflow has/needs a job-level timeout-minutes for queued jobs so maintainers get a clearer 'runner unavailable' signal instead of a generic failure.
prevention_strategies: Add monitoring/alerting on self-hosted runner pool queue depth and registration failures so a stuck-queue incident is caught and auto-remediated (e.g., restart the runner scale set) before it causes a hard failure on master. Consider a repository_dispatch or scheduled health-check that pings each self-hosted runner label periodically.
historical_context: No prior pattern for 'jobs stuck in queued state / runner pool exhaustion' category was found in the post-commit pattern database; this is the first recorded occurrence of this specific signature. Related but distinct patterns exist for Windows runner extraction failures (locked tbb12.dll, count=10; missing oneDNN license file, count=1) and network-related failures (artifact upload ENOTFOUND, codeload.github.com timeouts), all of which involve jobs that did start but then failed, unlike this run where jobs never started at all.
